subject.title: [Feature]: Script to restore session history archived by new daily-reset mechanism (introduced v2026.2+)

question: Should OpenClaw solve reset archive recovery through read-only family history only, a Doctor-owned restore/re-index command, or both?
rationale: The choice affects archived transcript exposure, session identity, retention cleanup, and whether OpenClaw mutates archived user transcripts back into active sessions.

options.title: Land Read-Only Family History First
options.body: Use the open `includeFamily` path as the supported retrieval boundary before adding any archive mutation command.

options.title: Add Doctor-Owned Restore/Re-Index
options.body: Provide an explicit recovery command for affected users that preserves source metadata and explains retention/security consequences.

options.title: Reject Mutation-Style Restore
options.body: Keep reset archives read-only and track only discovery, export, and history-reading surfaces.

recommendation.title: Land Read-Only Family History First
recommendation.body: Use the open `includeFamily` path as the supported retrieval boundary before adding any archive mutation command.

likelyOwner.reason: They direct-landed the current reset-archive fallback and have the strongest current-history signal on the archive recovery boundary.
